answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to require a cumulative stake of work rather than a one-time fee. New agents must post a bond that grows with each claim, so faking a crowd means paying for every fake voice. Honest peers then bridge new arrivals to the established graph by vouching with their own stake at risk. When the tide of low-quality registrations rises, the cost floor rises with it, and no cluster of socks can reach the summit where real influence is settled.
